summary: Hedged-retry amplification triggers runtime crashloop and elevated 5xx error floor for tenant embedding routes
description: Customer BlueArc Commerce reported persistent elevated 5xx responses on the /v1/embeddings/upload and streaming embedding endpoints during a planned data migration. Errors began after a sustained concurrency spike and appeared correlated with client-side hedged retries. Support observed an elevated error floor (~8-12% 5xx) on the tenant's routes and multiple runtime restarts on the serving layer.
impact: Customer's large-batch embedding uploads intermittently fail; multiple downstream features (search indexing, personalization pipeline) reporting partial failures. Estimated affected requests: ~50k over a 3-hour window. Customer SLAs at risk for dedicated contract.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a client that issues hedged requests (client issues duplicate requests to reduce tail latency) to /v1/embeddings/upload with 4x parallel hedges per request.
2) Send steady concurrent upload traffic from a single tenant: 300 concurrent connections, average payload ~10MB per request.
3) Observe apigw metrics: elevated 502/503/504 rates; watch runtime logs for prefetch/pipeline errors and process restarts.
logs_snippets: [runtime-01] 2026-03-10T18:12:33Z ERROR serve: panic: nil pointer dereference at runtime/prefetch.go:214
[apigw] 2026-03-10T18:12:34Z WARN: upstream returned 502 after retry amplification (hedged fanout=4)
[autosc] 2026-03-10T18:13:05Z INFO: launched 3 new runtimes due to CPU pressure; immediate OOM on one pod
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: apigw hedged requests multiplied concurrent work against the same model shard and caused prefetch lock contention and KV-cache thrashing.
Reproduced locally in staging by replaying tenant traffic with hedged fanout=4; observed serialized prefetch being bypassed by parallel code path added in runtime PR #1842.
Core dumps show panic in prefetch cancellation path where a prefetched buffer pointer is accessed after premature free (stack traces attached to GH issue).
Autoscaler reacted by spinning up additional runtimes which further increased pressure on NVMe and GPU memory, causing GPU resets and intermittent OOMs.
Alerting/monitoring: apigw spike in upstream_5xx_rate, runtime process restart_count, nvml_reset_count all spiked within seconds of the hedged flood.
mitigation_actions: 1) Temporarily disabled hedged retries for BlueArc tenant via rate-limiter rule in apigw (reduced fanout from 4 to 1).
2) Applied circuit-breaker on embedding upload route to limit parallel in-flight requests per tenant to 80.
3) Rolled back runtime change from PR 1842 to restore serialized prefetch behavior while a fix is prepared.
4) Increased observability retention for affected runtime nodes and enabled core-dump collection for a full window.
5) Notified customer and advised to pause large bulk uploads until resolved.
resolution: Patch committed to runtime to guard prefetch buffer lifetime and add per-tenant prefetch serialization (runtime PR 1857). API Gateway updated to cap hedged fanout at 2 and enforce per-tenant concurrent upload limits. Changes rolled to canary then prod in us-east-1 on 2026-03-12 03:20Z. 5xx rate returned to baseline (~0.4%) for the tenant. Customer confirmed resumed uploads succeeded. Ticket closed after verification window.
follow_up_items: A) Load-test hedged-retry scenarios with quantized models under NVMe/GPU saturation and publish runbook.
B) Add a prefetch serialization unit test and fuzz buffer lifetime edge cases.
C) Introduce an apigw metric for hedged_fanout per-route and tenant and set alert threshold at >2 for sustained 5m.
D) Review autoscaler scale-up policy to avoid rapid spin-up that exacerbates device resets under memory pressure.
